## What this dashboard shows

- Consolidated performance across Wipro Enterprises' three business segments (Consumer Care & Lighting, Infrastructure Engineering, Joint Ventures) drawn from five ERP systems (two SAP S/4HANA, Oracle EBS, Microsoft Dynamics 365, Tally Prime), before intercompany eliminations.
- Total Revenue of ₹2377.93B with EBITDA of ₹681.86B at a 28.7% margin (Healthy status).
- Total Expenses of ₹1696.07B representing 71.3% of revenue, split between Cost of Goods Sold at ₹1247.56B (52.5%) and Operating Expenses at ₹448.51B (18.9%).

## What to report

- Group revenue reached ₹2377.93B with year-to-date growth of +17.4% (Jan–Jul 2026 vs 2025), demonstrating strong top-line momentum.
- EBITDA margin of 28.7% (Healthy) reflects disciplined cost management, with Gross Margin at 47.5% (Healthy) after absorbing COGS of 52.5% of revenue.
- Operating expenses held to 18.9% of revenue (₹448.51B), keeping total expenses at 71.3% and delivering ₹681.86B in EBITDA.
- Performance spans seven legal entities across US, Australia, Germany, India, and Europe, plus two joint ventures (Wipro GE Healthcare at 49% and Wipro Kawasaki Precision Machinery at 51% ownership), reported at 100% ownership before eliminations.

## Watch out for

- Monthly P&L shows expense bars dipping below zero in Mar and May 2025 and Jan 2026 due to large credits in production activity, stock moves, inventory revaluation gains, and production variances in the real SAP company (Consumer Care International); matching costs land in other months, resulting in negative EBITDA in Jun–Jul 2025. Ask: Are production accounting entries correctly matched across periods?
- Figures are before intercompany eliminations; actual consolidated group results will differ. Ask: What is the IC elimination impact on revenue and EBITDA?
- Data includes simulated SAP records and simulated SAP S/4HANA alongside real SAP BDC. Ask: Which entities or periods rely on simulated data, and when will actual data be available?
- Joint venture entities reported at 100% ownership rather than equity stake (Healthcare 49%, Kawasaki 51%). Ask: What is the proportionate EBITDA contribution after applying ownership percentages?
